free_tier.stated: The Lightweight Core project package is free, with 15 build hours, 5 GB of backup storage and 100 GB of egress a month, but CPU, RAM and disk are billed separately against account credit: shared CPU USD 0.60 per core per 30 days, RAM USD 0.75 per 0.25 GB per 30 days, disk USD 0.05 per 0.5 GB per 30 days. Signup grants USD 15 in promo credits with no card, and a USD 10 payment verification adds USD 50 for USD 65 total.

egress.terms: Lightweight Core is Free with 15 hours build time, 5 GB backup storage and 100 GB egress per month; resource pricing Shared CPU USD 0.60 per CPU/30 days, RAM USD 0.75 per 0.25 GB/30 days, quoted
egress.free_allowance: 100 GB per month (Lightweight Core, free); 3 TB per month on Serious Core at USD 10 per month

record.interface_detail: zCLI (Linux, macOS, Windows) and a REST API with Bearer personal access tokens and Swagger; no SSH or SDK read on the pages
record.tooling: zCLI, the provider's command-line tool (Linux, macOS, Windows); the REST API (Bearer personal access token, Swagger) can also be called directly.
record.chaining: USD 15 of credit with no card buys a container plus a managed Postgres for three to five months, which is enough to finish and measure a project; the 100 GB monthly egress on the free core outlives the credit, so a static or cached workload can stay after the compute is gone.

limits.value: the USD 15 no-card credit is the whole free allowance: at the vendor's own estimate of USD 3-5 a month for a simple app with a database, that is about three to five months of one small project, and the free core package does not cover the containers.

The record does not state whether signup asks for an email address or a GitHub account, nor whether debit or prepaid cards are accepted for the optional USD 10 payment

record.interface_detail: GUI, import YAML, and a REST API; "Direct Port Access ... Protocols: TCP, UDP".
record.tooling: wg-quick on the service; the port is configured in the Zerops GUI or import YAML.
record.chaining: Zerops direct UDP port plus a wg-quick peer gives a tunnel endpoint; the 100 GB/month cap means it carries control traffic and fallback, not bulk transfer.

limits.value: 100 GB per month on the Lightweight Core

record.binding_note: At 1 TiB/month the free core's 100 GB/month egress is exceeded 11 times over; extra egress is $0.02/GB. The port itself costs nothing.

identity_cost.detail: Sign up at app.zerops.io; "You get $15 in promo credits on signup, no credit card needed." Verifying with a $10 payment is optional and adds $50.

record.reliability_note: Firewall rules are per port, blacklist or whitelist. No ban or throttle documented for direct ports.
record.confidence_note: A live UDP probe of a Zerops direct port, sending a WireGuard handshake and reading the reply, would raise this to measured.

evidence.proved: Direct Port Access: port range 10-65435, protocols TCP and UDP, IPv6 first or Unique IPv4 add-on

record.notes: Cloud platform providing container runtimes with public IPv6 networking. IPv4 addressing requires paid add-ons at USD 3 monthly.

extras.wg_detail: Direct Port Access: any port 10-65435, Protocols: TCP, UDP, mapped to an internal service port. wg-quick listens on that external port. IPv6 works without an add-on; a Unique IPv4 address is a $3.00/month add-on.
extras.volume_stated: Lightweight Core - Free: Egress Traffic: 100 GB per month.
extras.transit_note: Zerops public ingress carries the datagrams to the runtime container.
